digest.definition: An artistic and critical discipline centred on imagination, curiosity and the power of language, whose focus is generating ideas and expressing originality through literary, poetic or narrative forms
distinctiveFeatures: An artistic and critical discipline centred on imagination, curiosity and the power of language, whose focus is generating ideas and expressing originality through literary, poetic or narrative forms

Making texts sits at the centre: students develop their own creative practice and methods, drafting and redrafting, across many genres, forms and media, from print to performance, screen, audio, games and new forms
Originality is understood as emerging from the writer's own cultural, literary and personal contexts in dialogue with existing forms, influences and techniques
Learning is collaborative and workshop-based, with peer and tutor feedback at its heart, alongside independent study
Reading is broad and includes craft, criticism, theory and other media; projects may be creative-critical, and creative writing is itself a form of research
Highly interdisciplinary: studied alone or in many combinations, drawing on literature, drama, poetics, mythology, folklore, rhetoric and more
Strongly tied to the creative industries and wider careers, and to well-being and personal confidence in self-expression

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: inclusive learning communities and reading lists in line with the Equality Act 2010, belonging, participation plans in the four nations, external agencies tackling inequality in publishing and students defining their own canon of forms and voices; graduates show understanding of equality and engage with diverse writers and voices (D1, 1.21 to 1.26, 3.18, 3.19, 4.6)

many routes of entry, portfolio or presentation in place of written entry tests, accessible materials and spaces, prepared and adapted workshops, support for writing about personal themes and accessible assessment with alternatives (D1, 1.27 to 1.32, 3.17, 3.18, 3.22)

nature and environmental writing, the human and the more than human, ecological thinking through story and UNESCO's key competencies (critical, self-aware and anticipatory thinking); the rungs move from awareness to imaginative exploration to transformative writing on sustainability (D1, 1.33 to 1.38, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7)

careers in the creative industries and beyond, creative entrepreneurship, writing to commission and to briefs, with a list of enterprise skills the subject builds; the rungs move from awareness of applications to strategic transfer to new spaces for entrepreneurial expression (D1, 1.15, 1.16, 1.39 to 1.41, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5)

AI as content and tool: courses explore its limits and possibilities, analyse its effect on creative industries and use it to develop material with transparency; submissions may engage with AI; assessment of originality and methods may need to change; master's students weigh the ethics of using AI (D1, 3.9, 3.20, 3.26, 3.32, 4.7)

subjectSpecific.text: Through your studies you will become practised in what language and story can do expressively, imaginatively and emotionally, including structure and form.
Through your studies you will understand text, narrative and language as materials for art, each with its own history and possible uses.
Through your studies you will recognise the many ways readers and audiences may respond to and interpret your work.
Through your studies you will develop critical insight and the capacity to use it.
Through your studies you will practise editing your work over many drafts, on your own and with tutors and classmates, and see why it matters.
Through your studies you will appreciate the many creative and cultural settings in which writing is made and read.
At master's level, you use advanced creative and imaginative skill to conceive, design and produce a substantial writing project.
At master's level, you finish a large creative writing piece, of fitting length or form, that adds something original to its field.
At master's level, you write a critical piece on how your project began and developed, place it in a scholarly or creative tradition and show what is original about it.
At master's level, you use advanced analytical and imaginative skills to spot, define and solve the problems your writing project raises.
At master's level, you know in practice how you work, what influences you and how you approach writing, so you can adapt well to any creative challenge.
At master's level, you carry out your own research to support your project.
At master's level, you use advanced craft, editing and storytelling skills to move your work forward, respond to feedback from peers and tutors and trust your own judgement on how to make it better.
At master's level, you adjust your writing style to different media and narrative forms, and weigh the creative risks and gains of using technology.
At master's level, you evaluate, discuss, adapt and place your work in relation to wider social questions such as sustainability, diversity or the ethics of using AI to create.

At master's level, you turn complex and sometimes emotionally difficult material, observations and experiences into effective writing, using the right narrative and literary forms, for instance writing about people and place that changes how readers see other beings and the world around them.

transferable.text: Through your studies you will take responsibility for your own work, from the first idea through development and editing to the last draft.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to start your own work and take responsibility for it.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to present information professionally, in a way that suits the setting.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to manage yourself, work on your own, set goals, handle your workload and hit deadlines.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to see change coming, adjust to it and find your way through situations that are unclear, uncertain or new to you.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to reflect on your own development and identify your strengths and what you need to work on.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to choose and use digital and communication tools, and find, judge and manage information from many sources.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to write or tell a true story in clear or persuasive language, using your own experience or what others have told you.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to work flexibly, on your own and with other people.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to show and put to active use many transferable communication and storytelling skills.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to put your own and others' ideas across briefly, accurately and persuasively to change minds, building and presenting arguments in the right way.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to build your skill in listening actively and understand why it matters.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to communicate in different media, with a strong sense of how story, narrative and language work and what they are for.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to work well with others in teams and groups, for example in workshops or joint projects.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to show that you understand equality, diversity and inclusion.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to adapt to different demands and tasks and look past the immediate job to its wider setting, including the social and commercial impact of what you make.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to value both giving and receiving feedback.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to evaluate your work and reflect critically on your own practices and assumptions.
By the time you graduate, you should be able to grow more confident in the wider personal skills writing builds, such as self-expression and self-awareness.

At master's level, you manage yourself and your time, write independently and learn on your own, so that you can complete a major project, taking the initiative and deciding well when things are complex and unpredictable.
At master's level, you take part in analytical, critical group discussion and help solve problems in other writers' work.
At master's level, you give feedback sensitively, showing you grasp what the writer is trying to do and that different backgrounds and experiences shape how people judge good writing.
At master's level, you work in teams at an advanced level and respond to fast-moving cultural industries, to professional challenges and to global settings.
At master's level, you communicate well with experts and non-experts through advanced writing, speaking and storytelling.
At master's level, you use what you understand about writing as a life-enhancing skill to support your own and other people's well-being, confidence and self-expression.

statements.about: encouraging students to use peer feedback
statements.paraphrase: Peer feedback is a frequent and formative part of teaching in the subject; courses should encourage students to use these occasions to sharpen how they give and take feedback, usefully and with empathy.

forPractitioner.text: Build regular peer feedback into teaching and actively encourage students to use it to get better at offering and receiving critique that is both useful and kind.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course to encourage; the student-facing skill is in 4.4.b16 and 4.6.b16

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Creative Writing degree

statements.appliesTo: Creative Writing courses that use workshops
statements.about: extra preparation to make workshops accessible
statements.paraphrase: Workshops, where students read work in progress and peers respond, are common and open to critique; to make them accessible to every student, including disabled and neurodivergent students and those with chronic mental health conditions, further preparation is required.

forPractitioner.text: Workshops are valuable but not accessible by default: prepare them in advance so that disabled students, neurodivergent students and those with long-term mental health conditions can take full part, and weigh the critiques of the workshop model when designing them.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its tutors; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Creative Writing degree

statements.about: the resources of language and story
statements.paraphrase: Through study of the subject, students will reach experienced use of the expressive, imaginative and emotional resources of language and story, structure and form included.

forPractitioner.text: Students will, through the course, develop experienced use of the expressive, imaginative and emotional resources of language and story, structure and form included; make it visible in modules and assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: Through your studies you will become practised in what language and story can do expressively, imaginatively and emotionally, including structure and form.

forPractitioner.text: Students will, through the course, develop an understanding of text, narrative and language as materials for art, with their past traditions and possible uses; make it visible in modules and assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: Through your studies you will understand text, narrative and language as materials for art, each with its own history and possible uses.

forBeneficiary.text: Through your studies you will recognise the many ways readers and audiences may respond to and interpret your work.

forPractitioner.text: Students will, through the course, develop growth in critical insight and in the capacity to use it; make it visible in modules and assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: Through your studies you will develop critical insight and the capacity to use it.

statements.about: editing over successive drafts, alone and with peers
statements.paraphrase: Through study of the subject, students will reach practice in editing work through repeated drafts, on their own and with tutors and other students through peer review, and a grasp of why it matters.

forPractitioner.text: Students will, through the course, develop practice in editing work through repeated drafts, on their own and with tutors and other students through peer review, and a grasp of why it matters; make it visible in modules and assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: Through your studies you will practise editing your work over many drafts, on your own and with tutors and classmates, and see why it matters.

statements.about: creative and cultural contexts of writing
statements.paraphrase: Through study of the subject, students will reach an appreciation of the many creative and cultural settings in which writing is made and read.

forPractitioner.text: Students will, through the course, develop an appreciation of the many creative and cultural settings in which writing is made and read; make it visible in modules and assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: Through your studies you will appreciate the many creative and cultural settings in which writing is made and read.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Creative Writing degree

statements.about: progression across levels towards the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Across the honours degree (FHEQ level 6, FQHEIS level 10) a student will move up through the levels under each institution's rules, each level adding knowledge, expertise and experience towards meeting the threshold subject and generic skills, usually by completing and gaining credit for all learning and assessment.

forPractitioner.text: Plan each level so that it builds knowledge, expertise and experience towards the threshold subject-specific and generic skills in 4.3 and 4.6; students will normally progress by completing, and earning credit for, all learning and assessment, practical work included.

forBeneficiary.text: As you move up through the levels of your degree, you will build knowledge, skill and experience towards the minimum subject and general skills for honours, usually by passing and gaining credit for all your learning and assessment, practical work included.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Creative Writing degree

statements.about: core skills in joint and combined degrees
statements.paraphrase: Students taking the subject within a joint or combined degree will reach the core of its specific and generic skills, add others from their other subject and may work across the boundary between disciplines.

forPractitioner.text: In joint and combined degrees, make sure students will reach the core of the subject-specific and generic skills, let the partner subject add its own and use the overlap for interdisciplinary work.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study creative writing as part of a joint or combined degree, you will gain the core subject and general skills, add others from your other subject and may explore where the two meet.

statements.about: accessible assessment and clear policies
statements.paraphrase: Learning is supported by formative and summative assessment; assessment should be accessible to every student, alternatives should be offered to meet accessibility needs and the rules on extensions, late work and extenuating circumstances should be clear to all.

forPractitioner.text: Make every assessment accessible, offer alternative assessments where a student's access needs call for them and publish the extension, late submission and extenuating circumstances policies in terms every student can find and follow.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: performance above threshold; Annex D
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do clearly better than the threshold; each provider decides how such achievement is evidenced and should consult Annex D of the qualifications frameworks, which describes the four honours classifications.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to go well past the threshold; when setting how achievement above it is evidenced and classified, refer to Annex D's descriptions of first, upper second, lower second and third-class honours.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in judging classification; the student-facing rungs are 4.3 to 4.5

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: generating work and developing it by revision
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown, as the minimum for the honours degree, the capacity to produce creative writing and improve it through editing and redrafting.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every honours graduate will have shown the capacity to produce creative writing and improve it through editing and redrafting; make sure every passing student can evidence it.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum for your honours degree, you will produce your own creative writing and improve it by editing and redrafting.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: reflection on own creative process and outputs
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown, as the minimum for the honours degree, the capacity to think back over how they write and what they produce.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every honours graduate will have shown the capacity to think back over how they write and what they produce; make sure every passing student can evidence it.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum for your honours degree, you will think back over how you write and what you produce.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: engagement with own creative interests and influences

forPractitioner.text: By graduation, honours students should be able to work well with others in teams or groups, for instance in collaboration or workshops; give them chances to practise and evidence it.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate, you should be able to work well with others in teams and groups, for example in workshops or joint projects.

statements.about: understanding equality, diversity and inclusivity
statements.paraphrase: On graduating with honours, students should be able to show that they understand equality, diversity and inclusion.

forPractitioner.text: By graduation, honours students should be able to show that they understand equality, diversity and inclusion; give them chances to practise and evidence it.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate, you should be able to show that you understand equality, diversity and inclusion.

statements.about: adapting to demands; wider social and commercial effects
statements.paraphrase: On graduating with honours, students should be able to adjust to varied demands and tasks and see past the task in hand to its wider setting, including what their work does socially and commercially.

forPractitioner.text: By graduation, honours students should be able to adjust to varied demands and tasks and see past the task in hand to its wider setting, including what their work does socially and commercially; give them chances to practise and evidence it.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate, you should be able to adapt to different demands and tasks and look past the immediate job to its wider setting, including the social and commercial impact of what you make.

statements.about: value of giving and receiving feedback
statements.paraphrase: On graduating with honours, students should be able to value giving feedback and receiving it.

forPractitioner.text: By graduation, honours students should be able to value giving feedback and receiving it; give them chances to practise and evidence it.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate, you should be able to value both giving and receiving feedback.

statements.about: critical self-reflection on practice and assumptions
statements.paraphrase: On graduating with honours, students should be able to evaluate and reflect on themselves, critically examining their own practices and assumptions.

forPractitioner.text: By graduation, honours students should be able to evaluate and reflect on themselves, critically examining their own practices and assumptions; give them chances to practise and evidence it.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate, you should be able to evaluate your work and reflect critically on your own practices and assumptions.

statements.about: confidence in life-enhancing skills
statements.paraphrase: On graduating with honours, students should be able to show growing confidence in the wider personal skills the subject builds, for example self-expression and self-awareness.

forPractitioner.text: By graduation, honours students should be able to show growing confidence in the wider personal skills the subject builds, for example self-expression and self-awareness; give them chances to practise and evidence it.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate, you should be able to grow more confident in the wider personal skills writing builds, such as self-expression and self-awareness.

statements.about: advanced creative skills for a substantial project
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show advanced creative and imaginative skills that carry the conception, design and making of a substantial creative writing project.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show advanced creative and imaginative skills that carry the conception, design and making of a substantial creative writing project; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you use advanced creative and imaginative skill to conceive, design and produce a substantial writing project.

statements.about: composite professional skills for a substantial project
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show combined professional skills, managing themselves and their time, writing independently and learning on their own, needed to complete a substantial project with initiative and sound decisions when things are complex and unpredictable.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show combined professional skills, managing themselves and their time, writing independently and learning on their own, needed to complete a substantial project with initiative and sound decisions when things are complex and unpredictable; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you manage yourself and your time, write independently and learn on your own, so that you can complete a major project, taking the initiative and deciding well when things are complex and unpredictable.

statements.about: a substantial original piece of writing
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show the completion of a large creative writing piece, of suitable length or form, that adds something original to its field.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show the completion of a large creative writing piece, of suitable length or form, that adds something original to its field; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you finish a large creative writing piece, of fitting length or form, that adds something original to its field.

statements.about: critical writing on the project and its tradition
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show a critical piece on how their project arose and was carried out, setting it within a fitting scholarly or creative tradition and making clear what is original in it.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show a critical piece on how their project arose and was carried out, setting it within a fitting scholarly or creative tradition and making clear what is original in it; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you write a critical piece on how your project began and developed, place it in a scholarly or creative tradition and show what is original about it.

statements.about: analytical and imaginative problem-solving in a professional project
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show advanced analytical and imaginative skills for spotting, defining and solving the problems a professional writing project throws up.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show advanced analytical and imaginative skills for spotting, defining and solving the problems a professional writing project throws up; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you use advanced analytical and imaginative skills to spot, define and solve the problems your writing project raises.

statements.about: applied awareness of own process for adaptability
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show a practical grasp of how they work as writers, what influences them and how they approach writing, so that they adapt skilfully to any creative challenge.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show a practical grasp of how they work as writers, what influences them and how they approach writing, so that they adapt skilfully to any creative challenge; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you know in practice how you work, what influences you and how you approach writing, so you can adapt well to any creative challenge.

statements.about: independent research for the project
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show the capacity to conduct their own research to support the project.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show the capacity to conduct their own research to support the project; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you carry out your own research to support your project.

statements.about: advanced craft, editing and story skills; using feedback
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show advanced craft, editing and storytelling skills that move the work forward, including acting on feedback from peers and tutors and the confidence to judge for themselves how to make the project better.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show advanced craft, editing and storytelling skills that move the work forward, including acting on feedback from peers and tutors and the confidence to judge for themselves how to make the project better; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you use advanced craft, editing and storytelling skills to move your work forward, respond to feedback from peers and tutors and trust your own judgement on how to make it better.

statements.about: analytical group discussion and problem-solving on peers' work
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show the capacity to take part in analytical, critical group discussion, bringing problem-solving to bear on other writers' work.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show the capacity to take part in analytical, critical group discussion, bringing problem-solving to bear on other writers' work; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you take part in analytical, critical group discussion and help solve problems in other writers' work.

statements.about: sensitive feedback
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show the capacity to give feedback with sensitivity, for instance by showing a keen sense of what the writer is aiming for and weighing how varied backgrounds and experiences shape judgements of good writing.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show the capacity to give feedback with sensitivity, for instance by showing a keen sense of what the writer is aiming for and weighing how varied backgrounds and experiences shape judgements of good writing; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you give feedback sensitively, showing you grasp what the writer is trying to do and that different backgrounds and experiences shape how people judge good writing.

statements.about: adapting style across media; technology as a creative tool
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show skill in adjusting writing style to varied media and narrative forms, weighing the creative risks and gains of technology as a tool for making and representing.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show skill in adjusting writing style to varied media and narrative forms, weighing the creative risks and gains of technology as a tool for making and representing; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you adjust your writing style to different media and narrative forms, and weigh the creative risks and gains of using technology.

statements.about: positioning work within social challenges, including AI ethics
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show the capacity to evaluate, discuss, adapt and place their work in relation to wider social challenges such as sustainable development, diversity or the ethics of making work with AI and other new technologies.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show the capacity to evaluate, discuss, adapt and place their work in relation to wider social challenges such as sustainable development, diversity or the ethics of making work with AI and other new technologies; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you evaluate, discuss, adapt and place your work in relation to wider social questions such as sustainability, diversity or the ethics of using AI to create.

statements.about: transforming complex and difficult material into effective writing
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show the capacity to turn complex cultural material, and sometimes emotionally hard material, observation and experience, into effective creative writing with fitting narrative and literary forms and techniques, for example writing about people and place that changes how readers perceive other beings and their surroundings.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show the capacity to turn complex cultural material, and sometimes emotionally hard material, observation and experience, into effective creative writing with fitting narrative and literary forms and techniques, for example writing about people and place that changes how readers perceive other beings and their surroundings; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you turn complex and sometimes emotionally difficult material, observations and experiences into effective writing, using the right narrative and literary forms, for instance writing about people and place that changes how readers see other beings and the world around them.

statements.about: advanced teamwork in changing cultural industries
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show advanced teamwork, showing they can respond to fast-moving cultural industries, to professional challenges and to global contexts.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show advanced teamwork, showing they can respond to fast-moving cultural industries, to professional challenges and to global contexts; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you work in teams at an advanced level and respond to fast-moving cultural industries, to professional challenges and to global settings.

statements.about: communicating to specialist and non-specialist audiences
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show the capacity to communicate well with specialists and non-specialists, shown through advanced writing, speaking and storytelling.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show the capacity to communicate well with specialists and non-specialists, shown through advanced writing, speaking and storytelling; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you communicate well with experts and non-experts through advanced writing, speaking and storytelling.

statements.about: writing as a life-enhancing skill for well-being
statements.paraphrase: Students achieving master's level show the capacity to draw on their grasp of how creative writing can enrich lives to help themselves and others gain well-being, confidence, self-expression and self-awareness.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students show the capacity to draw on their grasp of how creative writing can enrich lives to help themselves and others gain well-being, confidence, self-expression and self-awareness; design the course and its final project so that they can.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level, you use what you understand about writing as a life-enhancing skill to support your own and other people's well-being, confidence and self-expression.
